missionPremise: _decisions/2026-08-18_smartcity_kit_component_package.md (active, amended same day before implementation). The SmartCity kit is ~109 CSS classes and 0 JS components, so a design agent cannot consume it; design sync converts a compiled component library. The package is a typed wrapper that renders existing kit classes and owns no styling.
completionPredicate: A stranger can install the built package, import a component for every class in the shipped vocabulary, render a screen that is markup-identical to the shipped product, and cannot express a token, a color, a radius, a duration, a bare number, or an absence with no basis through its API.
scopeBasis: Coverage is the WHOLE shipped vocabulary by operator ruling. Vocabulary is defined as the class set extracted from smartcity-dashboards@main web/sc-kit.css + web/shell.css, not from 30b section 3.9 (which lists the spec reference build's classes, a different and larger set). Reason: gate item 3 says a component's emitted class must exist in sc-kit.css or the product stylesheet, so the stylesheet set is the only set the gate can check.

vocabularyEnumeration.method: regex over comment-stripped web/shell.css + web/sc-kit.css from smartcity-dashboards@main
vocabularyEnumeration.countingRule: distinct class-selector tokens appearing anywhere in either stylesheet, including state modifiers (on, open, demo), element-scoped children (t, k, v, rail) and the two theme classes. Pseudo-classes, attribute selectors and element selectors are not classes and are not counted.

findings.severity: low, must be reported not silently absorbed
findings.claim: smartcity-dashboards web/sc-kit.css is NOT byte-identical to 30b section 4.1, so gate item 1 read strictly against 30b would fail on the very file the card orders copied verbatim.
findings.evidence: LF-normalized diff. 30b 4.1 = 3794 bytes, sha256 20e08faf61e449e075289cbfdfef146b894538bed3f6e0ef8adba7f16b4614f9. Shipped sc-kit.css = 4329 bytes, sha256 2cdd0bf876ee24224eb0e976c4c29f1f79bb37324a53aac50d3d78feec113ef2. Delta is exactly two hunks: an 8-line provenance header comment, and one added line declaring --sc-spring-stiffness:320, --sc-spring-damping:32, --sc-spring-mass:0.9 inside the final root block. Every token VALUE is identical.
findings.assessment: Not a fork. 30b section 1.7 names --sc-spring as stiffness 320 / damping 32 / mass 0.9; the shipped file expresses that one doc token as three CSS custom properties. Doc-vs-shipped expression drift, not a value change.
findings.disposition: The kit copies the shipped file, per the card. Gate 1 is enforced in three parts and part C pins this delta so any NEW divergence fails.
findings.routedTo: planner: 30b section 4.1 and web/sc-kit.css should be reconciled in one direction; the kit is not the place to fix it.

findings.claim: The planner estimate of 18 to 22 components is low by roughly 3x for 1:1 markup parity over 109 classes.
findings.evidence: Classes such as t, sub, k, v, n, nm, rail, gl, badge, st-k, sep, id, subj are element-scoped children of a parent class. Covering them 1:1 without inventing wrapper markup requires each to be a real component or a typed slot. Planned surface is 24 modules and roughly 65 exports.
findings.disposition: Report the real number with its counting rule rather than compressing the API to hit the band.

findings.claim: 30b section 3.9 names product classes that do NOT exist in the shipped stylesheets: sc, avatar, lensswitch, chip, filterbar, toast, ph, btn-danger, btn-icon, field, hint, kbd, seg, cite, cite.model, atomchip, basisline, meter, mx, mxgroup, mxrow, mx-pass, mx-fail, mx-unc, mx-unchecked, finding, gridlines, parcel, sheet, cp-card and its parts, cp-claim, cp-kv, cp-honest, cp-pop, cp-composer, cp-u, cp-a, p4bar, cz-top, cz-nav, cz-body, cz-card, phone.
findings.assessment: These live in the 30b reference build, not in smartcity-dashboards. A component emitting them would fail gate 3 by construction, because the class it renders exists in no stylesheet the consumer loads.
findings.disposition: Deliberately excluded, named in the close with this reason. This means the kit ships NO Cite, NO AtomChip and NO applicability-matrix component; those load-bearing 30b components have no shipped CSS to render against.

findings.claim: Shipping only sc-kit.css makes every component render unstyled for a consumer, because the component classes live in shell.css, not sc-kit.css.
findings.disposition: The package ships BOTH files as byte-identical copies, each hash-pinned and drift-tested against upstream. Neither is authored here. This satisfies gate 4 read as no CSS RULE OF ITS OWN while making the package usable. Flagged because the card named only sc-kit.css explicitly.

findings.claim: web/index.html emits class roster-lens, which appears in neither stylesheet.
findings.evidence: Five sections carry class="lens roster-lens". Not present in shell.css or sc-kit.css.
findings.disposition: The kit does not emit it; it would fail gate 3. The markup-parity comparison normalizes it out of the reference and the normalization is declared in the test.

componentToClassMap.plannedCoverage: 109 of 109 (100 percent), denominator = the 109 distinct class tokens above

lawEncodingDecisions: Law 3, quiet on satisfied and loud on unresolved: the Pill prop is named meaning, its values are the six semantic meanings, and it DEFAULTS to quiet. There is no variant, color, tone, emphasis, filled or strong prop, so there is no way to make a pill louder than its meaning. A test asserts a Pill with no props renders pill p-quiet; flipping the default to p-ok fails it.

Never-bare number: Metric is a discriminated union, either value plus note or unread plus note. note, the counting rule or basis, is required in BOTH arms, so a count cannot render without its rule and an unknown cannot render as a zero.
Honest absence: State REQUIRES kicker, heading and basis. An absence with no basis is a type error, not a review comment.
Section 1.6 elevation: Panel has no elevation, shadow or raised prop. A gate test asserts no exported component prop surface contains one.
Section 1.3 type ramp: the Text step prop is exactly the three steps the stylesheet ships (label, caption, data). No numeric size prop exists, so an off-ramp size is unrepresentable.
Prov requires source, rendered inside a b element. There is no shape that renders a value with no label.

gateTestDesign.gate1: Three parts. 1a: no --sc- declaration in any package-AUTHORED file (whole repo except vendor and dist). 1b: the only files carrying --sc- declarations are the two registered vendor files, each matching its pinned LF-normalized sha256. 1c: vendor/sc-kit.css differs from vendor/30b-section-4.1.css by EXACTLY the pre-registered F-1 delta; any other hunk fails.
gateTestDesign.gate2: regex scan of src for hex colors, rgb and rgba, px lengths, ms and s durations.
gateTestDesign.gate3: STRUCTURAL, not a hand list. Every export is rendered through examples/gallery in every variant, class attributes are parsed out of the rendered HTML, and each token is checked against the 109-class stylesheet set. A completeness test asserts every export of the package index appears in the gallery, so a component cannot dodge the check by being unregistered.
gateTestDesign.gate4: Every css file anywhere in the repo, excluding node_modules, must be registered in vendor/UPSTREAM.json and match its pin. An authored stylesheet fails by existing. Plus: no style element, no styled-components, no css tagged template, no css import in src.
gateTestDesign.eachWatchedFailing: required before close; recorded in CP2 with the verbatim failing output.

instrumentExclusions.lineEndings: All hash and byte-identity comparisons are over CRLF-normalized content. Reason: this repo is cloned on Windows with autocrlf, so raw-byte comparison would report drift that does not exist in git. The kit repo also carries .gitattributes eol=lf. This normalization is the instrument's declared exclusion and is stated where its output is read.
instrumentExclusions.vendorDirectory: vendor and dist are excluded from the AUTHORED-file scans (gates 1a and 2) by definition, since they are copies. They are INCLUDED in gates 1b, 1c and 4, which is what checks them.

risks: Upstream drift detection needs a smartcity-dashboards checkout. Pinned hashes survive a clone and catch edits to the copy; they do NOT catch upstream moving. Mitigation: CI checks out the public smartcity-dashboards repo and byte-compares for real, so the guardrail survives a clone per DEV_PROCESS 6.1. The repo has no CI today; adding it is part of this card.
Screenshot comparison is a human read of two images, not an automated pixel diff. The automated half is the markup-parity test against the vendored index.html. Stated rather than implied.
constraintsHonored: smartcity-dashboards cloned read-only and not modified
